title: Frontier-prefetch coordinator and compact index summarizer for tenant dashboard queries
creator: Maya Liang
description:
Problem:
Users are seeing long-tail tail latencies on tenant dashboard explorations (median OK, 99th percentile spikes when users page or open high-cardinality cohorts). Root cause analysis indicates a) high fan-out when stitching paginated queries across time buckets, b) cold micro-index reads for tenant-specific aggregates, and c) suboptimal read scheduling that forces many small seeks under load.

Goal:
Reduce 95/99p query latency for interactive dashboard endpoints by 30-50% under production load while keeping tokenized storage costs stable. Provide a low-risk rollout path with feature flags and safety fallbacks.

Proposal (high level):
1) Frontier-prefetch coordinator: a lightweight coordinator that observes query read frontiers (requested cursor windows) and issues speculative prefetches of adjacent shards/windows into an in-memory compact prefetch buffer. Prefetch decisions use tenant priority, recent access heatmap, and a short lived cost budget to avoid runaway IO.
2) Compact index summarizer: maintain per-tenant compact index summaries (bloom + top-k micro-index) that allow us to skip shards without full seeks. Summaries are small (few KB) and updated incrementally during background compactions.
3) Read hedging + backpressure: when coordinator detects long tail (sampled traces), it triggers hedged reads to warm replicas, and applies backpressure to low-priority background prefetches.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive prefetching reduces latency but can increase IOPS and memory; we set a cost budget per tenant and a global budget circuit-breaker.
- Compact summaries speed skips but add write amplification during compaction; we target off-peak compaction and opportunistic piggybacking during existing maintenance windows.
- Coordinator centralization vs. distributed decision: we implement coordinator as a lightweight per-shard controller co-located with query workers to avoid cross-shard coordination latency.

Success metrics (observability):
- 95p and 99p tail latency for /dashboard/query endpoints (target: -40% 95p, -30% 99p)
- Reduction in number of full-shard seeks per query (target: -60%)
- Prefetch hit rate in compact prefetch buffer (target: >70% for interactive flows)
- Bounded additional IO cost (target: <10% increase at peak)

Instrumentation & rollout plan:
- Feature gated under runtime flag console.prefetch.frontier and console.index.summarizer.
- Canary rollout to 5% of tenants (low-traffic cohort) with realtime SLO dashboards and anomaly alerts.
- Regression tests: synthetic workload harness reproducing tenant patterns (large cohorts, deep pagination) running in CI with comparison against baseline.
- Metrics emitted: prefetch.requests, prefetch.bytes, prefetch.evictions, summary.size_bytes, summary.update_latency, hedged_reads.count, query.seek_counts, query.latency_pxx.

Implementation notes and rough tasks:
- Proto: coordinator in query-worker (Go) that subscribes to per-query read-window hints (existing cursor protocol extension). (Arjun)
- Compact summarizer: implement incremental bloom and top-k sketch in storage compactor (Rust component) with API to expose to query workers. (Jamie)
- Budgeting and circuits: integrate with central quota service (authored by infra) to limit global prefetch IO. (dependence on ENG-30482 for quota adapter)
- Instrumentation: add tracing spans to correlate prefetch -> query latency (Maya)

Rollout checkpoints:
- Prototype + microbench (local): 2025-02-21
- Internal review (arch + storage): 2025-02-28
- Canary start: 2025-03-07
- Canary evaluate: 2025-03-14
- Full rollout pending results: by 2025-03-21

Notes on backward compatibility:
- Feature is opt-in; if summarizer unavailable for a tenant we fall back to legacy read path.
- Prefetch is non-blocking: queries don't wait for prefetch completion; it's used to serve subsequent adjacent reads.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: prefetch causes spike in IO causing noisy neighbor effects. Mitigation: per-tenant cost caps + global circuit-breaker + rapid disable via feature flag.
- Risk: summaries stale cause missed skips. Mitigation: conservative skip thresholds and a TTL-based fallback to full reads.

Deliverables:
- New coordinator module in query-worker (Go) + unit/integration tests
- Summarizer integration in compactor + gRPC fetch path for query-worker
- Canary dashboard and alert runbook
- RFC doc and design diagrams (links below)
comments: 2025-02-13 Maya L: Triage complete. Confirmed reproducible on prod replay. Created synthetic harness to simulate tenant paging patterns (link in artifacts).

2025-02-18 Arjun P: Spike done — simple prefetch buffer prototype reduced simulated 95p by ~28% on median fanout workloads. Memory overhead within budget for small buffer sizes. Posting prototype results: github.com/redwood/prototypes/prefetch-spike PR#312.

2025-02-24 Jamie R (storage): Design review notes — summarizer should use a 64-bit fast hash and target 2-4 KB per tenant to be acceptable. Also recommend update of compactor to emit summary diffs to avoid full recomputation.
2025-03-01 PM review (Evan S): Approved for canary after adding circuit-breaker telemetry and runbook. Added requirement to include customer impact tagging for canary cohorts.

2025-03-04 Arjun P: Integration branch open (github.com/redwood/query-worker PR#478). Basic coordinator + budgeter wired. Running CI perf harness now. Next: wire compactor endpoint and add canary flagging in console config.
